summary: Three more articles in myseliasan's built-in manual, in all four shipped languages (12 files), taking it to 18 articles per language. Users, roles and access explains the property the page is built on: a new sign-in arrives with NO role and sees an access-pending screen rather than the control plane, because authenticating proves who somebody is and does not say what they may see -- plus disabling rather than deleting a departed colleague, retiring the stock superadmin via the bootstrap handoff, the viewer default for a new role, features-before-paths access, longest-prefix-wins with deny-by-default, and the fact that MENUS AND API PERMISSIONS ARE THE SAME MATRIX (a menu switch grants GET on that section's path, so a role can never see a page it cannot call and hiding a menu is not a measure applied on top of a real one -- it is the real one). Node access is documented as the separate question it is. The audit log covers the append-only record, what each column means, that DENIED attempts are recorded too (a refused action is evidence, and a log of only successes could not tell the two situations apart), System as a genuine non-human actor, and using it to tell a released node from a self-dropped one from one that is merely offline. The settings editor covers save-then-restart and why applying mid-request would change the rules under sessions already in flight, the safe subset (the database, server and bootstrap settings are deliberately NOT editable from the app that needs them to run), blank-means-unchanged for secrets, per-section restore defaults, and config.json as the recovery path when a change stops the app starting. Also fixes a stale UI string in all four languages: the Users page claimed every sign-in is provisioned as a viewer, which contradicts the shipped pending-clearance behaviour the tests assert.
compatibility: Backward compatible. The manual articles are content only -- markdown compiled in by the existing //go:embed and served by the manual endpoints that already exist; anchors are identical across all four languages and every cross-link resolves, so the conformance suite and the contextual-help drift guard both still pass. One user-visible string changed (rb.usersHint, in en/ms/zh/ar) to describe what the software actually does. Two defects were fixed in the shared retrieval tokenizer (domain/shared/manual/retrieval), which affects ranking for every app that uses it: suffix rules now CASCADE, since applying only one left 'settings' at 'setting' while 'setting' went on to 'sett' so the two never matched, and 'changed' reached 'chang' while 'change' stayed 'change' -- a stem that drops a silent e now also emits the restored form; and contracted negations (won't, can't, doesn't) are dropped whole rather than split on the apostrophe, which had left 'won' in the index where it matched 'who won the football'. Both are ranking-quality changes with no API or storage impact; the index is rebuilt in memory on every start, so there is nothing to migrate.
